key_insight: Two-qubit Pauli-Z correlation matrices from any quantum state are automatically feasible for the classical Goemans-Williamson relaxation, creating a quantum-to-classical certification bridge for optimization and circuit analysis.
engineering_relevance: This gives variational quantum algorithms a built-in performance certificate for Max-Cut-style objectives and enables polynomial-time circuit cutting using only low-order correlation data.
method: Map the quantum state’s degree-2 moment matrix into the GW semidefinite relaxation.
Apply GW random hyperplane rounding to obtain a certified expected cut value.
Use the same correlation matrix to detect tensor-product structure and choose near-optimal circuit partitions for cutting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical validation on Max-Cut instances and random states, showing near-optimal bipartition detection and agreement with the theoretical error bounds.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on two-point correlation information and the quality of the moment-based partitioning, so practical performance may depend on measurement noise and problem structure.
paper_title: Certifying Quantum Optimization and Circuit Cutting by Using Quantum-Classical Moment Duality
